text.p: Dutch builder NBM-Amstelland NV said on Thursday net profits almost doubled in 1996 thanks to a strong profit contribution from newly-consolidated Cementbouw and earnings growth in all its divisions except housing.
"With the exception of the housing construction group, all divisions and particularly Cementbouw contributed to the doubling of profit," NBM said in a statement.
The builder earlier reported 1996 net profits mushroomed to 81.5 million guilders from a year-earlier 40.8 million.
Profits per ordinary share (after preference dividend) rose 19.7 percent to 2.85 guilders from a year-earlier 2.38 guilders.
Building materials trader Cementbouw, acquired in 1995, was fully-consolidated for the first time in 1996.
NBM said housing construction again booked a disappointing result in 1996, but that drastic restructuring in various areas coupled with cost savings should help restore profitability.
Turnover at the company's project development and real estate arm jumped some 15 percent but operating profits lagged those of last year.
However the profit contribution of NBM's shareholding in property funds Capa City Realty and Germany's GFG boosted the division's net result, NBM said.
